description: Story Phase 7 (the Great Sharkstorm returns; the Song of the Grand Stenchmaster) has begun: two days after Phase 6.
Cleared the storm debris midships.
Re-rove the fore shrouds with Finch.
Ned, at the bow: 'It's... bigger, Captain. Isn't it?'
Fins in the air, high, over the ship, going the wrong way for fins.
Spray on the deck, tinged yellow.

THE GREAT SHARKSTORM HAS RETURNED: not destroyed, only disrupted and pushed away, it reorganised out of the contamination in the air and the sea and the hundreds of sharks still following the Revenge, and came back. (Permanent.)
THWACK. The first shark on the deck again. Squawks: 'No.' 'I know.'
A tiny wisp off the Grand Stenchmaster. 'He's still smoking.' 'That is not smoke.'
RESIDUAL STENCHMASTER EXHAUST (forbidden by the captain), renamed GRAND STENCHMASTER AURA (worse). (Permanent.)
Chapter 34: Which Away?
Port main shrouds made fast.
Starboard fore shrouds made fast.
The mainsail reefed.
Squawks inside the captain's coat, buttoned in, head out, for the rest of the storm.
A shark coming down forward of the main hatch, its shadow growing.
A shark landed forward of the main hatch.
Hands on the deck shark, lifting.
The deck shark heaved over the side.
'Which way, Captain?' 'AWAY.' 'Which away?' 'That is an excellent question.'
The Grand Stenchmaster is furious, about his television: Franklin has an audit hearing tonight. (Recorded episodes: 'Grand Stenchmaster technology.')
Chapter 35: Not a Stenchmaster Duty.
The captain took the emergency labour rule down off the mainmast to read it to him.
The loophole: the Great Sharkstorm is Meteorological Shark Management, outside the reasonable operational scope of the Grand Stenchmaster.
Hale chalked it up: WHAT DOES HE DO? Not allowed: wear the suit, fart, watch television, be lazy.
THE GRAND SHARKMASTER: an office Garrick invented in an argument, to manage the sharks his own office produces. Vacant. Not real. (Permanent; recurring.)
Chapter 36: The Job Description.
Gristle's grievance: he invented the title, and the suit, and the duties.
Pete's grievance: the contamination, the treasure, the rum, the beard.
Bob's grievance: the sharks. All the sharks.
Hale's grievance: the second release, and what came out of it.
Rook's grievance: now he won't help because a different imaginary department should.
'Everything on your list is something you want to do anyway.' 'Excellent career alignment.'
A flying shark took a great piece of the Grand Stenchmaster's painted cape (and a tassel). His suit is torn, dented, stained and crooked now. He thinks it's magnificent. (Permanent.)
'GET THAT SHARK BACK.' 'Then what is the crew for?' The crew went for him; he ran.
Chapter 37: The Grand Stenchmaster's Parade.
The Grand Stenchmaster Ceremonial Parade began (the captain ordered him not to; he couldn't hear over the storm).
Helped Pete get a shark over the side. ('I'm assisting emotionally.' 'THEN EMOTIONALLY PULL!')
Helped Bob tie off a line. (Garrick's cuffs, which are already soaked in Frog Grog.)
Helped Salty Jim with a crate. ('It's food.' Garrick interested. 'No.')
The Grand Stenchmaster's ceremonial parade: once round the deck in a storm of sharks, saluting, ordered not to. (Permanent.)
Chapter 38: The Song of the Grand Stenchmaster.
The Song of the Grand Stenchmaster: one verse, a chorus and half a second verse, until the captain stopped it. Squawks hid. (Permanent.)
'Now I must get back to work.' (The television.)
A second shark finished the original S.E.S.; Garrick took what was left. Wrecked, kept, stripped. (Permanent.)
Garrick took the compass out of the binnacle ('You've been steering AWAY').
Garrick took the wire off the storm lantern by the cabin door ('It wasn't doing anything').
The lantern fell off its hook. 'SEE?' 'Now it's definitely free.'
Garrick took the lucky horseshoe off the cabin door ('Reception').
Chapter 39: Everyone Below.
The wheel lashed, as well as it can be.
The main hatch barred from below. Nobody goes up on deck while the Great Sharkstorm sits over the ship.
Everyone in the hold: the strongest part of the ship.
Chapter 40: The Stenchmaster Entertainment System Mark II.
The old aerial from Mark I. Cartoon zap. 'Is he dead?' 'No.' 'Unfortunate.'
SPECIAL INSULATION (a sock soaked in Frog Grog). 'THAT MAKES IT WORSE.'
Signal routing: a horseshoe and a fork. 'There is no routing.' 'There is now.'
A knob tied on with string. Not connected. 'Looks professional.'
The S.E.S. Mark II is built: a turnip crate, the old tube, mismatched tubes, a horseshoe, a fork and a spoon. (Permanent.)
The captain kept Garrick's hand off the switch (once).
The captain kept Garrick's hand off the switch (twice).
'Maybe some noise would help.' Garrick took it as authorisation.
Mark II's startup: nothing, nothing, FLASH, an orange tube, a suspicious blue one, clicking, hum, sparks, a line, snow. 'WARM-UP.'
Through the static: 'Ribbit...' FRANKLIN RETURNS.
The S.E.S. Mark II works. It shouldn't. It receives The Frog Tax Man. (Permanent.)
Chapter 41: A Pleasant Evening.
Season seventeen, the flies: business snacks or personal snacks? Bob laughed. Then Gristle watched. Then Pete.
The captain counted the crates instead (twice).
The captain tried to get some sense out of the crew (they shushed him).
The captain checked the bilge pump (fine).
A shark hit the hull, and the captain sat down. 'Do not claim this.'
The whole crew watched The Frog Tax Man together, in the hold, during the Great Sharkstorm. (Permanent.)
Several pirates are now fans of Franklin the Frog, despite themselves. (Permanent.)
The compromise: the Grand Stenchmaster will see about the storm after ONE episode. (The captain's sword was involved.)
Squawks: 'Frog better Stenchmaster.' The captain laughed, for the first time in days.
To Franklin. To surviving. To one day throwing the television overboard. (Everyone gagged but Garrick.)
A pleasant evening in the hold: the crew rested, more or less.
Story Phase 7 is complete.
The captain has looked at the S.E.S. Mark II up close.
The captain has looked at the back of Mark II (SIGNAL (PROBABLY); DO NOT LICK).
The captain has looked at Mark II's power source (a lantern's glow, a bottle of Frog Grog, the spare bell, a garter).
Mark II responds to a slap on the crate (never the horseshoe).
The captain found Garrick's lyric sheet (with the crew's contributions written in).
